text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli prime minister: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat has done "damn all".
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, peace envoy Dennis Ross discuss peace process.
- West Bank, Jerusalem security boosted.
- Congress not expected to renew law on U.S. ties with the PLO before summer recess.
- Builders ban all Palestinian labour; bar applies even to those with work permits.
- Bombing cost put at 3.5 million shekels ($1 million).
- Chief scientist woos U.S. investors.
- Tecnomatix Technologies to clean Chernobyl.
GLOBES
- Accord between state and management: 7.5 percent of Bezeq shares will be issued and 2.5 percent will be sold in sales proposal.
- Delay expected in presentation of price proposals in Bank Hapoalim tender.
- Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky says events won't affect investors.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: There's no link between the attacks and the condition of the peace process. Possibility Albright will make Middle East trip.
- Syrian army chief: If the Golan Heights are not returned by way of peace -- security forces will get them back for us.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Prime Minister: The Shin Bet has a "green light" to act in Palestinian areas. "I expect the PLO to be expelled from Washington".
MAARIV
- Netanyahu accuses Arafat of allowing "timebomb" to operate against Israel.
- Netanyahu will meet the finance minister this morning to discuss economic steps to increase economic growth.
- Increased military and police presence in city for fear of further attacks.
- Gallup poll before the attack: Overwhelming majority of Israelis back significant compromises with the Palestinians.
